tpPageHero.label: TRANSFER PRICING
tpPageHero.title: When Value Moves Across Borders, Transfer Pricing Matters.
tpPageHero.description: For multinational businesses, transactions between related entities are part of everyday operations. Goods are supplied. Services are provided. Intellectual property is used. Financing moves between companies. Functions, assets and risks are distributed across jurisdictions.
tpPageHero.aside: Each of those arrangements can have transfer pricing consequences.

tpCommercial.text: Parker Russell member firms provide transfer pricing expertise to international businesses seeking to understand, structure, document and defend their intercompany arrangements across multiple jurisdictions.
tpCommercial.body: Our approach considers not only the numbers attached to a transaction, but the business activity behind them — how value is created, which entities perform the relevant functions, where assets are used, how risks are managed and whether the resulting transfer pricing position can withstand scrutiny.

rightColumn.text: Transfer pricing should reflect how the business actually operates.

tpWhy.title: An Internal Transaction Can Create an External Tax Risk.
tpWhy.lead: Transactions within a group may happen between related companies, but their tax consequences are very real.
bodies: As businesses expand internationally, tax authorities increasingly need to understand how profits are allocated between jurisdictions and whether related-party transactions reflect the economic activity taking place.

A transfer pricing position that is not properly designed or documented can create uncertainty, adjustments and disputes — particularly when different tax authorities examine different parts of the same international structure.

card.title: That makes transfer pricing more than a documentation exercise.
card.label: It requires businesses to understand the relationship between:

steps.text: and how that position can be supported.

tpWhy.conclusion: The stronger the connection between commercial reality and transfer pricing, the stronger the position behind it.

tpCritical.title: International Growth Changes the Transfer Pricing Picture.
tpCritical.lead: Transfer pricing becomes increasingly important as the number, scale and complexity of transactions within an international group grow.

cards.title: Entering New Markets
cards.description: Establishing entities or operations in another jurisdiction can introduce new intercompany relationships and transfer pricing requirements.

cards.title: Changing the Group Structure
cards.description: Acquisitions, reorganisations and changes in operating models can alter where functions are performed, assets are used and risks are managed.

cards.title: Increasing Intercompany Transactions
cards.description: Growing volumes of goods, services, financing, intellectual property or other related-party transactions can increase both complexity and exposure.

cards.title: Developing Intellectual Property
cards.description: Where intellectual property is developed, owned or used across jurisdictions, understanding the underlying functions and economic relationships becomes particularly important.

cards.title: Financing Across the Group
cards.description: Intercompany loans and other financial arrangements can create transfer pricing considerations around pricing, terms and the commercial basis of the arrangement.

cards.title: Facing Greater Tax Scrutiny
cards.description: When tax authorities examine related-party transactions, businesses need a position that is supported by appropriate analysis and documentation.

tpDesign.title: A Strong Transfer Pricing Position Has to Work at Every Stage.

stages.label: 01 — DESIGN
stages.title: Build the Position Around the Business.
stages.lead: Transfer pricing begins with understanding how the group actually operates.
questions: Which entities perform the important functions?
Where are risks assumed and managed?
How do entities contribute to the creation of value?
texts: The answers provide the economic foundation for considering how related-party transactions should be structured and priced.
stages.emphasis: A transfer pricing policy that does not reflect commercial reality may become difficult to support regardless of how extensive the documentation is.

stages.label: 02 — DOCUMENT
stages.title: Make the Rationale Clear and Supportable.
stages.lead: Documentation should explain more than the result.
texts: It should provide a coherent basis for understanding the relevant transactions, entities, functions, economic circumstances and transfer pricing approach.
Parker Russell member firms can bring relevant local expertise to documentation requirements within their jurisdictions while considering the wider international structure of the group.
stages.emphasis: The objective is a transfer pricing position that can be understood, evidenced and consistently applied.

stages.label: 03 — DEFEND
stages.title: Be Ready to Explain the Position Under Scrutiny.
stages.lead: Transfer pricing positions may be examined by tax authorities long after the underlying transactions have taken place.
texts: A defensible position therefore requires more than documentation prepared simply to satisfy a filing requirement.
stages.emphasis: The commercial rationale, economic analysis and supporting evidence need to tell a consistent story.

principles.text: Be prepared to defend the result.

cards.title: Transfer Pricing Risk Assessment
cards.description: Understanding where transfer pricing exposure exists across an international group.
cards.descriptionSecondary: The assessment considers current or proposed intercompany arrangements, the jurisdictions involved and whether the wider transfer pricing system appropriately reflects the commercial and economic relationships within the business.

cards.title: Transfer Pricing Policy & Framework
cards.description: A coherent transfer pricing framework provides a basis for how related-party transactions are approached across the organisation.
cards.descriptionSecondary: The objective is to connect transfer pricing policy with the group's operating model rather than treating pricing as a separate tax exercise.

cards.title: Intercompany Transactions
cards.description: Different transactions can create different transfer pricing considerations.
cards.descriptionSecondary:
Goods. Services. Financing. Intellectual property. Management and support arrangements.

Understanding the nature and economic purpose of each transaction is fundamental to determining an appropriate approach.

cards.title: Economic & Functional Analysis
cards.description: Transfer pricing requires an understanding of what each entity actually contributes.
cards.descriptionSecondary: Functions performed, assets used and risks assumed provide important context for assessing the economic relationship between related parties.

cards.title: Transfer Pricing Documentation
cards.description: Clear documentation provides evidence of the basis on which a transfer pricing position has been established.
cards.descriptionSecondary: For international groups, this also requires consideration of the requirements applicable within relevant jurisdictions.

cards.title: Transfer Pricing Review
cards.descriptionSecondary:
A transfer pricing approach established several years ago may no longer accurately reflect how the organisation operates today.

Periodic review can identify where changes in functions, transactions, markets or group structure have altered the transfer pricing position.

tpValue.title: Transfer Pricing Starts With Understanding Where Value Is Created.
tpValue.lead: A legal structure shows where companies are incorporated.
bodies: It does not necessarily explain where economic activity takes place.
To understand an international group's transfer pricing position, it is necessary to look beneath the organisational chart.
tpValue.structureLabel: The structure tells you where the entities are.
tpValue.analysisLabel: The analysis explains what they actually do.

dimensions.label: FUNCTIONS
dimensions.text: What activities does each entity actually perform?

dimensions.label: ASSETS
dimensions.text: Which tangible and intangible assets are used to create value?

dimensions.label: RISKS
dimensions.text: Which entities assume and manage economically significant risks?

dimensions.label: PEOPLE
dimensions.text: Where are important activities and decisions actually carried out?

dimensions.label: TRANSACTIONS
dimensions.text: What is being transferred between related entities — and why?

dimensions.label: VALUE
dimensions.text: How do those contributions connect to the economic outcome?

tpChallenge.title: One Group. Multiple Tax Authorities.

principles.text:
A transaction between two related companies connects at least two entities — and potentially two different tax systems with different documentation requirements, administrative practices and areas of scrutiny.

For larger international structures, the number of interconnected relationships can grow quickly.

The challenge is therefore not simply to establish an appropriate position within one jurisdiction.

It is to understand how that position fits within the group as a whole.

texts: Through Parker Russell International, independent member firms can collaborate where transfer pricing matters extend across jurisdictions, combining relevant local knowledge with a wider view of the international structure.

tpChanges.eyebrow: 07 — WHEN THE BUSINESS CHANGES, TRANSFER PRICING MUST FOLLOW
tpChanges.title: Yesterday's Policy May Not Reflect Today's Business.

consequence.title: Each change can alter the economic relationships between group entities.
consequence.text: A transfer pricing framework therefore needs to remain aligned with how the organisation actually operates — not simply how it operated when the original documentation was prepared.
consequence.statement: If the business changes, the transfer pricing analysis may need to change with it.

tpProcess.ariaLabel: From transaction to transfer pricing position
tpProcess.eyebrow: 08 — FROM TRANSACTION TO TRANSFER PRICING POSITION
tpProcess.title: Understand the Transaction Before Pricing It.

steps.label: 01 — IDENTIFY
steps.description: Which related-party transactions exist across the group?

steps.label: 02 — UNDERSTAND
steps.description: What is the commercial purpose and economic substance of each arrangement?

steps.label: 03 — ANALYSE
steps.description: Which functions are performed, assets used and risks assumed by the relevant entities?

steps.label: 04 — ASSESS
steps.description: How should the transaction be considered from a transfer pricing perspective?

steps.label: 05 — DOCUMENT
steps.description: What evidence and documentation are required to support the position?

steps.label: 06 — REVIEW
steps.description: Does the approach remain appropriate as the business and regulatory environment evolve?

tpProcess.conclusion: A defensible position begins with understanding the transaction itself.

tpRisk.title: Risk Often Sits in the Gap Between Policy and Reality.
bodies: A group may have a transfer pricing policy on paper.
The more important question is whether actual business activity continues to reflect it.
tpRisk.imageAlt: Illustration of transfer pricing policy versus business reality

triggers.text: intercompany arrangements evolve but documentation does not;
functions or decision-making move between entities;
new intellectual property is developed or used;
actual conduct differs from documented arrangements;
or different parts of the group apply the policy inconsistently.

tpRisk.note: That is why Parker Russell's existing Transfer Pricing Process focuses specifically on assessing current or future transfer pricing systems against the principles of designing, documenting and defending a position across multiple countries.
tpRisk.conclusion: The question is not only whether a policy exists. It is whether the position behind it can be supported.

tpPosition.ariaLabel: What a strong transfer pricing position requires
tpPosition.eyebrow: 11 — WHAT A STRONG TRANSFER PRICING POSITION REQUIRES
tpPosition.title: Technical Analysis Is Only One Part of the Position.

pillars.title: Commercial Understanding
pillars.description: Transfer pricing needs to reflect how the business actually creates value and operates.

pillars.title: Economic Analysis
pillars.description: The financial and economic substance of related-party arrangements needs to support the approach taken.

pillars.title: Local Knowledge
pillars.description: Requirements and areas of scrutiny can differ between jurisdictions.

pillars.title: International Perspective
pillars.description: Individual transactions need to be understood within the wider structure of the multinational group.

pillars.title: Consistency
pillars.description: Policy, documentation and actual business conduct should tell the same economic story.

pillars.title: Forward Thinking
pillars.description: Changes in the business should be considered before they create inconsistencies in the transfer pricing position.

tpFinal.ariaLabel: Build a transfer pricing position that can stand up to scrutiny
tpFinal.title: Build a Transfer Pricing Position That Can Stand Up to Scrutiny.
tpFinal.description: A strong transfer pricing framework should do more than satisfy a documentation requirement.
tpFinal.note:
It should reflect how the business operates, provide a coherent basis for related-party transactions and remain supportable as the organisation grows and changes.

Parker Russell member firms combine local tax knowledge with international collaboration to help businesses understand and assess transfer pricing risk across the jurisdictions in which they operate.
tpFinal.tagline:
Design it around the business.
Document it around the evidence.
Defend it with confidence.
